claim: Relaxation tests on pig heart and beef show Kelvin-Boltzmann and Hunt-Crossley both capture transient tissue behavior well; Kelvin-Boltzmann is selected for an Active Observer controller for accuracy, physical meaning, linearity, and stability-analysis convenience, not because Hunt-Crossley is universally inadequate.
epistemic_status: Model comparisons, controller results, and limitations are author-reported; implications for model sufficiency and optimal impedance are bounded inferences.
problem_and_setting: Selection of a real-time soft-tissue interaction model and force controller under breathing and heartbeat disturbances, using ex-vivo pig-heart and beef relaxation data and in-vitro control experiments.
method_or_mechanism: Six elastic/viscoelastic models are cross-validated. Kelvin-Boltzmann is embedded in a model-based Active Observer. Online adaptation updates only stiffness beta; disturbance estimation compensates physiological motion.
content_summary: Kelvin-Boltzmann and Hunt-Crossley best capture fast transients, while the fractional model fits relaxation but is nonrecursive and poorer in fast response. The controller reports stable static/moving behavior and 87% breathing and 79% heartbeat compensation. Aggressive observer tuning reduces stability margins and noise limits it; full online parameter estimation, convergence, and in-vivo validation remain open.
synthesis_role: Direct model-selection and force-control prior showing that HC inadequacy cannot be assumed and that model choice depends on accuracy, identifiability, and controller tractability.
development_link: A stronger problem is whether measurable memory or finite-area state changes optimal impedance decisions under held-out conditions, with HC and Kelvin-Boltzmann compared under equal identification budgets.

evidence.finding: Kelvin-Boltzmann and Hunt-Crossley are the strongest transient models in cross-validation.
Kelvin-Boltzmann is selected for controller accuracy, physical parameters, linearity, and tractable stability analysis.
A model-based Active Observer force controller is formulated and analyzed.
In-vitro tests report stable behavior with 87% breathing and 79% heartbeat compensation.
Noise and stability margins limit observer aggressiveness; only stiffness is adapted online and full estimation/in-vivo tests remain future work.

boundary_conditions: Ex-vivo pig heart and beef plus in-vitro control.
Smooth interaction may not excite viscosity.
Observer tuning trades compensation against stability and noise.
No optimal impedance, finite-area wrench, or explicit safety constraint is evaluated.
assumptions: The observer captures physiological motion as a disturbance.
Stiffness-only adaptation suffices for the reported tests.
Available excitation and noise bound identifiability.

reported: Fractional dynamics are nonrecursive and weak in fast transients.
Aggressive observer tuning erodes stability margins.
Noise limits tuning and viscosity may be insufficiently excited.
Full online estimation and in-vivo validation are absent.
inferred: The results refute blanket HC inadequacy.
Stiffness-only adaptation may confound memory mismatch and disturbances.
Reported compensation does not imply force, pressure, passivity, or tissue-safety guarantees.

conflicts_with: Any claim that HC uniformly fails on soft-tissue transients.
Any claim that constitutive fit alone determines the best control model.
Any claim that full viscoelastic parameters are identifiable online during smooth contact.

problem_lead_search_contexts.lead_statement: Hunt-Crossley may be an inadequate environment model for optimal impedance when soft contact exhibits decision-relevant relaxation, creep, hysteresis, or rate history that cannot be represented by current penetration and penetration rate alone.
problem_lead_search_contexts.purpose: Attempt to disconfirm the adequacy of memoryless Hunt-Crossley contact by locating direct soft-tissue force-control evidence for relaxation, creep, hysteresis, or frequency dependence and the control consequences of including or omitting memory.
problem_lead_search_contexts.expected_close_condition: Establish whether history-dependent viscoelasticity causes a measurable, decision-relevant control failure in the target regime and define the rate/hold conditions under which Hunt-Crossley remains sufficient.
